subject: Limit on Liability — annualized fee multiplier vs. total fees (MSA + Order Form)

Subject: MSA redlines (liability / damages)

Markus / Laura,

Attached is Acme's redline of the MSA and the Order Form. Two points our CFO/legal team raised that we need to resolve before we can proceed to signature: 1) the liability cap calculation — Acme is asking for a multiple of annual fees (2x of the prior 12 months) rather than a lifetime fees total; 2) consequential damages carve-outs for consumer-facing services.

Specifically, the redline proposes: liability limited to the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $1M, and carve-outs for willful misconduct/gross negligence and IP indemnity. They also want an explicit exclusion for lost profits and consequential damages except where required by law.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether you have flexibility on 2x vs 1x multiple?

Michael

Michael — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. We're aligned on moving quickly. High level position from Redwood: we prefer a liability cap tied to fees paid (to reflect commercial exposure) but need to keep it bounded for enterprise risk — our standard asks are either (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) a flat $2,000,000 floor for certain enterprise customers. We typically push back on multipliers >1x because that can balloon exposure.

Karthik (cc'd) — can you weigh in on whether we can offer a 1.5x annual multiplier as a compromise, and whether carve-outs for data breach/indemnities should sit outside the cap?

Markus Klein
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com; laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines (liability / damages)

Folks — quick legal note: Redwood's standard liability structure for Enterprise deals is: cap = the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) $1,000,000; carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and IP indemnity (these are uncapped). For regulated customers or strategic deals we can consider a floor increase to $2M or a 1.5x multiplier, subject to approval.

On whether indemnities and certain statutory obligations (data protection obligations, regulatory fines) sit outside the cap: we typically keep IP indemnity and intentional torts outside, but data breach liability generally stays subject to the cap unless there is willful misconduct. If Acme insists on uncapping data breach, we need to quantify and price that risk.

I can support a 1.5x annualized-fee multiplier as a one-off concession if Sales commits to a 2-year minimum in the Order Form and accepts an additional 0.25% price uplift to offset risk.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Michael Torres <m.torres@acme.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Offer: compromise on liability ceiling and Order Form commitments

Michael / Jane — following internal review, Redwood can propose the following compromise for the MSA and Order Form:

- Liability cap: the greater of (A) fees actually paid by Acme in the 12 months immediately preceding the claim, or (B) USD 1,500,000 (floor).
- Multiplier: instead of a flat multiplier, the parties agree the cap equals 1.5x of the prior-12-month fees, capped at a maximum of USD 4,000,000 for any single claim or series of related claims.
- Annualized approach: the 1.5x calculation is applied to the trailing 12-month fees measured at the time the claim arises.
- Carve-outs (uncapped): willful misconduct and IP indemnity.
- Data breaches: damages arising from a data breach remain subject to the liability cap unless Redwood is found to have engaged in gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Term/commitment trade: in exchange for the 1.5x multiplier and elevated floor, Redwood asks Acme to: (i) sign a 24-month minimum term in the Order Form; and (ii) accept a 0.25% uplift to the list price for the first 12 months to offset tail risk.

We think this splits the difference between your 2x ask and our standard 1x. If that sounds close, we can incorporate language into the redline and share an updated doc.

Best,
Markus

---

From: counsel@wilsonpierce.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com; m.torres@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 13:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Offer: compromise on liability ceiling and Order Form commitments

Markus — on behalf of Acme, thanks for the thoughtful counter. A few notes from legal: Acme's commercial team needs an explicit annualized approach (they want predictability for budgeting) and they prefer a 2x multiplier but are open to a capped multiplier. Concerns from our side: (1) the $1.5M floor is lower than expected for an account of Acme's size; (2) the 0.25% uplift needs to be formally documented and tied to the Order Form pricing schedule; (3) data breach carving-in under the cap will need clear definitional limits (e.g., exclusions only apply for Redwood's gross negligence).

Proposed redline language to insert into Section 9 (Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Provider's aggregate liability for any claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) 1.5 times the fees paid by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and (ii) One Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (USD 1,500,000); provided, however, that in no event shall Provider's liability for all claims in any consecutive twelve (12) month period exceed Four Million United States Dollars (USD 4,000,000). The foregoing limitation shall not apply to liability resulting from Provider's willful misconduct or Provider's indemnification obligations for third-party claims alleging intellectual property infringement. Damages for data breach shall be subject to the foregoing limitation unless Provider's conduct rises to the level of gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Please confirm and we will circulate an updated redline reflecting the 1.5x/cap language and the price uplift mechanics.

Regards,
Samantha Pierce
Wilson & Pierce LLP (external counsel for Acme)
